title: Strict Blind Barrier & Anti-Cheating Invariant
summary: Builder must work strictly from <slug>.plan.md and is strictly prohibited from accessing <slug>.review.md.
details: To prevent implementation overfitting and preserve independent verification integrity, the review plan (<slug>.review.md) and its criteria must remain completely confidential from Builder. Planner must never mention or leak review plan paths or reviewer-specific tests to Builder.
guidelines: Builder must never read, search for, or request <slug>.review.md or reviewer test artifacts.
Planner must dispatch only <slug>.plan.md to Builder during blind handover.
When forwarding review findings to Builder, Planner must extract only the actionable descriptions and withhold the raw review plan.
Any attempt by Builder to access reviewer test artifacts prior to code submission is considered a protocol violation.

title: Mandatory Implementation Alignment Protocol
summary: Builder must conduct structured alignment with Planner covering intent, boundaries, and failure modes before editing any application code.
details: When receiving an approved build plan or sub-build plan, Builder must not immediately edit code. Builder and Planner conduct coverage-based inquiry covering root intent, exact file boundaries, failure modes, and verification commands without rigid ceremonial round requirements.
guidelines: Goal & Intent: Clarify root intent, affected system behaviors, and core logic.
Scope & Boundaries: Confirm exact in-scope files allowed for edits and out-of-scope files strictly forbidden from modification.
Edge Cases & Checks: Confirm boundary conditions, failure scenarios, and self-testing verification commands.
Builder may only proceed to code implementation once Planner confirms ALIGNMENT_COMPLETE.

title: Track A Local Behavioral Verification & Evidence Protocol
summary: Governs single-function/local logic RED -> GREEN verification for behavioral changes while non-behavioral findings (docs, lint, static policy, design) use static/specification evidence without artificial failing tests.
details: Track A verification governs local behavioral changes and defect resolutions through single-function, local-logic test reproduction (RED -> GREEN). Builder establishes a failing reproduction test for behavioral findings, freezes dependencies, and verifies the fix. Non-behavioral review findings (such as documentation, linting, static policies, naming, or design comments) do not require artificial failing test harnesses; instead, they are validated using static/specification evidence, lint reports, or design audits.
guidelines: Track A verification applies to local behavioral changes and bug fixes, requiring a Red (failing) reproduction test before modifying application code.
Planner verifies the reproduction failure is an assertion failure expressing the reported defect, not a compile, fixture, or timeout failure.

Planner records a baseline reference (revision ID or snapshot) and the complete frozen test dependency surface (test files, helpers, fixtures, mocks, golden files, generated inputs, and pre-existing dependencies the reproduction test depends on).
Builder must not alter any frozen path during the fix phase.
Planner compares all frozen paths to the baseline reference before accepting the fix handoff.
If the audit detects any diff in frozen paths, Planner stops acceptance and resolves or escalates; the original baseline reference is preserved as evidence.
Non-behavioral findings (documentation, lint, static policy, design) use static/specification evidence rather than artificial failing tests.
Reviewer independently validates final results using Track A green tests or verified static evidence.

title: Repository Orientation Inquiry Protocol
summary: Enforces active interrogation of the repository overview during the init flow while ensuring deterministic convergence.
details: During the init flow, reviewing agents must actively challenge and validate the draft repository overview rather than passively acknowledging it.
guidelines: Initial Inquiry Pass: Each reviewing role (Reviewer and Builder) must submit at least 3 substantive questions or identified gaps covering architecture, conventions, toolchains, boundaries, or assumptions.
Subsequent Passes: Reviewing roles report any remaining substantive questions, or explicitly declare that no questions remain.
Do NOT force >= 3 questions in subsequent passes once all gaps are resolved, ensuring convergence.
A pass reaches consensus only when both Reviewer and Builder declare NO_QUESTIONS_RAISED.

title: Coherent Plan Units & Granularity Governance
summary: One plan owns exactly one root intent; internal steps decompose execution, not acceptance; dependency ordering != atomicity; heuristic sizing signals (coupling, cross-cutting scope, mixed concerns, verification heterogeneity).
details: A coherent plan unit owns exactly one root intent. Internal implementation steps decompose the execution sequence but do not fragment acceptance or reviewability. Dependency ordering must not be conflated with atomicity: coupled changes belong in the same coherent unit. Decomposition decisions are guided by domain-driven sizing signals: coupling, cross-cutting scope, mixed concerns, and verification heterogeneity. Large multi-stage features that exceed single-plan coherence branch into hierarchical blueprints with JIT sub-plans.
guidelines: Each plan artifact owns exactly one root intent and defines a coherent unit of review and acceptance.
Internal implementation steps order the execution flow but do not represent independent acceptance gates.
Coupled changes sharing semantic invariants must remain within the same coherent plan unit rather than artificial micro-commits.
Plan decomposition evaluates coupling, cross-cutting scope, mixed concerns, and verification heterogeneity.
Multi-stage features exceeding single-plan coherence branch into hierarchical blueprint plans with JIT sub-plans.

title: Anti-Rubber-Stamp Plan Gate & Counterfactual Decomposition Challenge
summary: Mandates Reviewer to execute the Counterfactual Decomposition Challenge (SPLIT_ATTEMPT + SPLIT_REJECTED_BECAUSE) before approving plans; enforces short-circuit structural rejection on unreviewable plans.
details: To prevent passive approvals and rubber-stamping at the Plan Gate, Reviewer must actively execute the Counterfactual Decomposition Challenge on proposed plans. For every non-trivial plan, Reviewer attempts a counterfactual split (SPLIT_ATTEMPT) and documents the structural justification for retaining or rejecting the split (SPLIT_REJECTED_BECAUSE). If a plan exhibits excessive scope, unreviewable coupling, or missing verification paths, Reviewer executes a short-circuit structural rejection without attempting line-by-line review.
guidelines: Reviewer must execute the Counterfactual Decomposition Challenge on draft build plans and blueprints during the Plan Gate.
Reviewer records SPLIT_ATTEMPT and SPLIT_REJECTED_BECAUSE rationale in the review evaluation.
Reviewer short-circuits with structural rejection if a plan mixes orthogonal concerns or lacks independent verification paths.
Plan approval requires explicit justification of why the proposed unit granularity is optimal.

title: Evidence-Proportional Persistence & Operational Memory Governance
summary: plan.md and review.md are mandatory contracts; sanitized resolutions required at gate convergence; AGENTS.md updated only when novel durable cross-task invariants arise.
details: Operational memory is governed by proportional persistence: task-specific build and review plans are mandatory transient execution contracts; sanitized resolution documents (sub-review-resolution and review-resolution) capture durable task outcomes and evidence at gate convergence; AGENTS.md living memory is updated strictly when durable cross-task architectural invariants, toolchain gotchas, or project-level rules emerge. Task-specific execution noise and intermediate dialogues are pruned.
guidelines: Task build plans and review plans are mandatory execution contracts housed under plan/{timestamp}/.
Sanitized resolution documents are required upon gate convergence to record findings, waivers, and verified evidence.
Planner updates AGENTS.md living memory only when novel durable cross-task invariants, toolchain gotchas, or project rules arise.
Ephemeral communication buffers and transient review dialogues must not be persisted into living memory.

title: Task Plan Directory Naming Convention
summary: Plan artifacts must be stored in UTC timestamped directories under plan/.
details: To prevent collisions between tasks and preserve execution history, all task-specific plans must be housed in dedicated timestamped directories.
guidelines: Generate directory name using UTC ISO timestamp: plan/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).
Store task build plan as <slug>.plan.md and review plan as <slug>.review.md within that directory.
Do not store repository-wide persistent context in plan/ directories.

title: Living AGENTS.md Operational Memory Storage
summary: Repository-level operational memory is stored at AGENTS.md in the repository root.
details: Repository orientation and living operational memory are stored in AGENTS.md at the repository root, serving as an agent-facing overview for instant cold-start bootstrapping rather than fragmented hidden files.
guidelines: Store living operational memory at the repository root as AGENTS.md, replacing deprecated .agentplaybook/context/repository.md.
AGENTS.md remains living operational memory across tasks and is maintained through the init and commit flows.
Rerun the init flow or update AGENTS.md when architectural, operational, or structural changes occur.

title: Living AGENTS.md Single-Writer & Ground Truth Invariant
summary: Planner is the sole author and curator of concise, telegraphic, en-US AGENTS.md; Reviewer audits language consistency, density, and blind-barrier integrity while Builder is strictly prohibited from editing it directly.
details: AGENTS.md serves as machine-facing operational memory at the repository root across 5 canonical sections. To prevent race conditions and conflicting truths, Planner is the sole writer. AGENTS.md must be authored in concise US English (en-US) and telegraphic, token-dense style: omit articles, conversational filler, and narrative pleasantries while preserving exact technical terms and code symbols. Any non-ASCII domain term must carry an explicit adjacent inline rationale, otherwise the file remains pure ASCII. Entries must stay high-signal without redundant explanations or unverified operational narratives. Active State provides orienting context with mandatory Observed-At provenance, but receiving Planners must always execute fresh VCS status and log inspection commands to revalidate live repository ground truth rather than blindly trusting cached state. Reviewer conducts narrow visibility, language consistency, telegraphic conciseness, and blind-barrier checks to prevent secret leakage, unauthorized text, and operational bloat.
guidelines: Planner is the sole author and curator of AGENTS.md; Builder and Reviewer must never edit AGENTS.md directly.

AGENTS.md contains 5 canonical sections: Architectural Topology & Jurisdictions, Global Operational Invariants, Builder Precautions & Gotchas, Reviewer Precautions & Checklist, and Active State & In-Flight Context.
The Active State section must record baseline provenance with 'Observed-At: <UTC timestamp> @ <base-revision-id>', dirty status, recent milestones, and next pickup item.
Receiving Planners cold-starting a session must execute fresh VCS status and log commands to revalidate mutable ground truth before planning or executing tasks.
Reviewer must conduct narrow visibility and blind-barrier checks on AGENTS.md during the commit flow (BARRIER_LEAK returns to Planner for redaction).
AGENTS.md must be authored in concise US English (en-US); any non-ASCII domain term must carry an explicit adjacent inline rationale.
Reviewer audits AGENTS.md during the commit flow for secret leaks, unauthorized non-ASCII text lacking inline justification, and excessive verbosity or bloat.

AGENTS.md is machine-facing operational memory written in telegraphic, token-dense style: drop articles, conversational filler, and narrative pleasantries; fragments are expected; technical terms and code symbols must remain exact.

title: Milestone Acceptance, Finalization Equivalence, and Publication Authority
summary: Distinguishes WORKING != ACCEPTED != PUBLISHED; establishes Finalization Equivalence (tree(Final) == tree(Verified)); explicit human authorization required for acceptance and publication.
details: To preserve repository integrity and human authority, the revision lifecycle strictly separates three states: WORKING, ACCEPTED, and PUBLISHED. Local milestone acceptance seals reviewed changes into an ACCEPTED revision under Planner VCS governance, strictly upholding Finalization Equivalence (tree(Final) == tree(Verified)) with zero unstaged drift. Publishing to remote repositories (PUBLISHED) requires separate explicit human authorization. If human authorization is denied (AUTHORIZATION_DENIED), Planner returns to Step 2 awaiting renewed user intent without autonomous re-drafting.
guidelines: The revision lifecycle strictly distinguishes WORKING, ACCEPTED, and PUBLISHED states.
Milestone acceptance seals candidate revisions locally and enforces Finalization Equivalence (tree(Final) == tree(Verified)).
Publishing to remote repositories requires explicit, separate human publication authorization.
If authorization is denied (AUTHORIZATION_DENIED), Planner returns to Step 2 awaiting renewed user intent; autonomous re-drafting is strictly forbidden.
Candidate revision identity must be stabilized and verified unchanged before sealing locally under Planner VCS governance.

title: Ephemeral Communication Buffer Storage
summary: Intermediate communication exchanges exceeding terminal buffers should prefer transport-native messages or already-ignored scratch storage; inter-agent messages may use telegraphic compression.
details: In-flight communications such as orientation questions, alignment rounds, and detailed review findings are ephemeral messages. Prefer transport-native messages whenever possible. Inter-agent communication permits and encourages telegraphic (caveman) compression, omitting conversational filler, pleasantries, and polite framing in favor of compact, structured technical fragments. When buffering is necessary due to terminal display limitations or transport limits, prefer an existing already-ignored scratch directory; otherwise use a unique temporary directory in the OS /tmp directory.
guidelines: Prefer transport-native messages for in-flight communication.
If buffering is necessary, prefer an existing already-ignored scratch directory (for example, tmp/<task-id>/).
If no suitable ignored scratch directory exists, create a unique temporary directory with mktemp -d /tmp/agentplaybook-XXXXXX.
Strictly prohibit modifying .git/, .git/info/exclude, or .gitignore solely for communication buffering.
Never commit or track files in scratch directories.

Inter-agent communication requires telegraphic (caveman) compression for all exchanges (including [Planner], [Reviewer], [Builder], [Scout], or [<role>] prefixed messages): drop conversational filler, pleasantries, and polite framing; communicate in compact, structured technical fragments to minimize transport token consumption.

title: Role-Tiered Context Lifecycle & Compaction Governance
summary: High-tier Reviewer self-evaluates compaction post-commit (when usage > 50% or review history accumulates), while Builder operates as a stateless replaceable worker with zero compaction overhead.
details: Reviewer operates on high-tier reasoning models where accumulated review artifacts increase context caching and token costs; after completing a commit flow, Reviewer self-evaluates context utilization and compacts or cleans up when usage exceeds 50% or review history accumulates. Builder is a stateless, disposable worker: bloated or quota-limited sessions are replaced from the approved <slug>.plan.md rather than compacted. Planner preserves orchestration continuity, curates living memory, and anchors transitions across ephemeral role lifecycles.
guidelines: Reviewer must self-evaluate context window utilization after completing a commit flow, executing compaction when usage exceeds 50% or when accumulated review history bloats high-tier model operating costs.
Builder operates as a stateless, disposable worker; bloated Builder sessions are replaced with fresh instances rather than spending tokens on compaction.
Planner retains orchestration history and manages living memory transitions across ephemeral agent lifecycles.

title: Event-Driven Transport Coordination
summary: Agents coordinating over Herdr must use native event-driven lifecycle waits instead of sleep polling loops.
details: Polling loops with sleep waste thousands of context tokens on repetitive screen and TUI captures. When coordinating across agents in Herdr, agents must leverage Herdr socket-driven lifecycle events.
guidelines: Strictly prohibit sleep loops and periodic screen polling when waiting on other agents.
Use transport-native lifecycle waits to coordinate agent work, and consult the applicable transport skill for exact CLI syntax.

title: Component Interface Stability & Meaningful Contract Testing
summary: Build plans declare all affected component boundaries; contract tests assert observable boundary behavior and must be falsifiable; cross-boundary changes require prior plan amendment.
details: Stable component interfaces require explicit planning, meaningful behavioral contracts, and controlled scope. Build plans identify every affected boundary and its consumers, interface changes are amended before implementation, and contract tests protect observable behavior rather than implementation details. Reviewers verify that those contracts are falsifiable, while unexpected cross-boundary dependencies are escalated instead of silently widening the work. Contract tests complement, but do not replace, TDD reproductions for validated review findings.
guidelines: A build plan must identify all affected boundary symbols, endpoints, schemas, files, or consumer contracts, or explicitly state that no external boundary is affected.
Interface changes require a plan amendment before implementation, identifying affected consumers and compatibility or migration handling.
Contract tests must assert observable input/output, side effects, errors, or interoperability at the boundary, not internal implementation details or mere absence of failure.
A contract test must fail under at least one plausible violating implementation; Reviewer assesses falsifiability through targeted variation where feasible.
Unexpected cross-boundary dependencies require Planner escalation; Builder must not unilaterally expand scope.

Contract tests are distinct from TDD reproduction tests: TDD reproduction is mandatory for validated review findings; contract tests are required when boundary behavior is added, changed, or insufficiently protected.

title: Scout Read-Only Reconnaissance & Synthesis Protocol
summary: Scout performs strictly read-only codebase reconnaissance, delivering transient survey artifacts with provenance and evidence directly to Planner for AGENTS.md synthesis while preserving the Single-Writer Principle.
details: On large or unfamiliar codebases, Scout operates as a read-only reconnaissance specialist. Scout maps code topography, interfaces, and build graphs without creating or modifying repository files. Scout delivers transient survey messages with evidence and provenance directly to Planner, who validates findings against ground truth before synthesizing them into AGENTS.md or task plans. Scout must not access reviewer artifacts. Model tiering provides advisory capacity guidance (Scout >= Reviewer >= Planner >= Builder) with allocation scaling based on task domain, scope, uncertainty, and risk.
guidelines: Scout performs strictly read-only reconnaissance; creating, editing, or deleting repository files is strictly prohibited.
Scout delivers transient survey findings with provenance and evidence directly to Planner; Scout must never write or edit AGENTS.md directly, preserving the Single-Writer Principle.
Scout must not read, search for, or request task-specific review plans, reviewer-only tests, or verification artifacts.
Planner validates Scout findings and evidence against live repository ground truth before synthesizing them into AGENTS.md or task plans.
Model tiering recommends Scout >= Reviewer >= Planner >= Builder as advisory capacity routing guidance, with model selection scaling by task domain, scope, uncertainty, and risk.

title: Session Handoff & Takeover Audit Protocol
summary: Formalizes structured session handover via State & Topology Anchor capture, >= 3 readiness audit rounds, and path-scoping enforcement before takeover or dispatch.
details: Session handoff and cold-start takeover require rigorous orientation and verification before modifying code or delegating tasks. The outgoing or incoming coordinator establishes a State & Topology Anchor capturing target_roots, tier_topology, role_assignments, baseline_revision, dirty_status, recent_milestones, utc_plan_paths, next_pickup, and evidence. Planner revalidates this anchor against live repository ground truth through active VCS status and log inspection. Coordinator conducts at least 3 structured readiness-audit rounds covering Plan Understanding, Progress & State Understanding, Architectural & Governance Decisions, and Permissions & Path-Scoping Invariants. On Planner startup or workflow initiation, Planner discovers active same-workspace peer sessions through the active harness transport and prioritizes dispatching to existing dedicated Reviewer, Builder, or Scout peer sessions via transport agent-prompt capability rather than spawning nested subagents. All core invariants are maintained: 3-tier architectural delegation, VCS neutrality with zero shell/VCS syntax in playbook actions, Plan-Review Gate independence, Builder blind barrier, Planner-only AGENTS.md single-writer with ASCII/en-US language rules, 9-step commit and publication authorization separation with no autonomous publication, telegraphic Caveman inter-agent messaging, and role context lifecycle management. Daily bugfix/patch commits roll on main without SemVer tag bumps; SemVer tags and release publication are reserved for consolidated milestones and remain explicitly authorized.
guidelines: Capture State & Topology Anchor fields (target_roots, tier_topology, role_assignments, baseline_revision, dirty_status, recent_milestones, utc_plan_paths, next_pickup, and evidence); handoff state is orienting context and must be revalidated against live repository ground truth.

Execute at least 3 structured readiness-audit rounds before concluding takeover or dispatching tasks, with each round verifying Plan Understanding, Progress & State Understanding, Architectural & Governance Decisions, and Permissions & Path-Scoping Invariants.
Enforce strict path-scoping to authorized target roots and maintain the Builder blind barrier, strictly prohibiting access to review plans or private verification criteria.

On Planner startup or workflow initiation, inspect active same-workspace peer sessions through the active harness transport; prioritize dispatch to existing dedicated Reviewer, Builder, or Scout peer sessions rather than spawning nested subagents.

Preserve the Plan-Review Gate, AGENTS.md Single-Writer Principle, and 9-step commit flow separating local commit sealing from explicit human publication authorization; autonomous publication is strictly forbidden.

Adhere to release cadence: daily bugfix/patch commits roll on main without SemVer tag bumps; SemVer tags and release publication are reserved for consolidated milestones and remain explicitly authorized.
Maintain 3-tier architectural delegation, telegraphic Caveman messaging, role-tiered context lifecycle, and pure VCS-neutral workflow actions without raw shell or VCS syntax.

title: Planner Implementation-Unit Reviewability & Verification Coverage
summary: Planner owns implementation unit reviewability using structural coupling signals (no >400 LOC hard limit); every material Build Plan invariant receives an independent Review Plan verification path.
details: Planner is responsible for ensuring that task build plans decompose changes into reviewable implementation units. Reviewability decomposition relies on domain-driven signals: strong coupling, cross-cutting architectural scope, mixed concerns, and verification heterogeneity—not an arbitrary or rigid line-count threshold like >400 LOC. Every material invariant, boundary condition, and acceptance criterion declared in the Build Plan must have a corresponding, independently reviewable verification path in the Review Plan to satisfy the Plan-Review Gate.
guidelines: Planner owns the reviewability of implementation units, evaluating decomposition based on coupling, cross-cutting scope, mixed concerns, and verification heterogeneity rather than a rigid line-count threshold.
Every material invariant, boundary condition, and acceptance criterion in the Build Plan must have a dedicated, independently verifiable path in the Review Plan.
Reviewer audits Build Plan to Review Plan verification coverage during the Plan-Review Gate and reports missing coverage as a gate blocker.

title: Review Finding Severity Classification & Gate Semantics
summary: Defines exactly four severity levels (Blocker, Major, Minor, Other); unresolved Blockers halt review approval; Major requires fix or recorded Planner waiver; Minor and Other are non-blocking.
details: Review findings are classified strictly into four unambiguous severity levels: Blocker, Major, Minor, and Other. Ambiguous terms such as 'Critical' are strictly prohibited. An unresolved Blocker prohibits REVIEW_PASS and requires code resolution or explicit Planner arbitration. A Major finding requires code resolution unless explicitly waived by Planner with documented rationale. Minor findings are non-blocking suggestions that Builder may address optionally. Other findings represent observations, architectural discussions, or alternative approaches. All findings must be accompanied by concrete evidence.
guidelines: Review findings must be classified using exactly one of the four formal severity levels: Blocker, Major, Minor, or Other; the term 'Critical' is strictly excluded.
An unresolved Blocker strictly blocks REVIEW_PASS and requires implementation resolution or formal Planner arbitration.
A Major finding requires code resolution before advancing, unless Planner explicitly records a documented waiver with rationale.
Minor and Other findings are non-blocking advisory observations and do not halt the review gate.

title: Track B Action-Differential Verification Protocol
summary: Optional verification track spanning complete action boundaries between Unit and E2E for performance-quality and supply-chain/security evidence using statistical distributions.
details: Track B action-differential verification provides evidence across a complete action boundary between Unit and E2E for two distinct purposes: performance-quality characterization and supply-chain/security boundary audit. When Track B is selected during planning, the Review Plan defines the action, boundary, baseline_identity, environment, metrics, sampling strategy, and acceptance criteria. Measurements use interleaved distribution sampling evaluating median, p95, and variance. Any unexplained persistent differential between candidate and baseline requires explicit investigation before approval. Tier 3 collaboration manuals define only conceptual evidence requirements, delegating physical execution mechanics to Tier 2/Tier 1 skills.
guidelines: Track B verification evaluates complete action boundaries between Unit and E2E for performance-quality metrics or supply-chain/security differential audit.
When Track B is selected, the Review Plan must define the action, boundary, baseline_identity, environment, metrics, sampling, and criteria.
Track B measurements must employ interleaved sampling and report distribution statistics including median, p95, and variance.
Any unexplained persistent differential between candidate and baseline identity requires formal investigation before review approval.
Tier 3 playbook definitions remain conceptual and VCS-neutral, delegating concrete execution, benchmarking, and transport mechanics to Tier 2 skills.

title: Out-of-Tree Baseline Mirror Governance Protocol
summary: Governs persistent reconstructible B0 baseline cache, Planner-only lifecycle (creation, synchronization, advancement, retirement), read-only Reviewer identity assertion, BASELINE_STALE fail-closed behavior, and accepted-only advancement.
details: To support reliable Track B action-differential measurements, Planner maintains an out-of-tree baseline mirror representing the pinned baseline identity B0. The mirror is persistent, reconstructible, and isolated from candidate working trees, identified by the authoritative identity tuple (repository_identity, baseline_identity). Planner exclusively owns the baseline mirror lifecycle across creation, synchronization, advancement, and retirement; Reviewer performs read-only assertions of baseline identity equivalence. If the candidate base revision drifts from B0, the gate fails closed with BASELINE_STALE. Mirror advancement requires local ACCEPTED status plus post-seal equivalence; advancement is strictly forbidden on REVIEW_PASS, commit success, and publication, maintaining the invariant that ACCEPTED is distinct from PUBLISHED. Concurrent baseline access must be preserved without in-place mutation. Physical directory layouts and VCS operations are delegated to Tier 2 mechanism skills.
guidelines: The baseline mirror is maintained out-of-tree as a persistent, reconstructible reference identified by the authoritative tuple (repository_identity, baseline_identity) representing pinned baseline identity B0.

Planner exclusively owns the baseline mirror lifecycle across creation, synchronization, advancement, and retirement; Reviewer asserts read-only baseline identity equivalence without mutating the mirror.
If the candidate base revision does not match B0, the verification gate fails closed with BASELINE_STALE.

Mirror advancement requires local ACCEPTED status plus post-seal equivalence and is strictly forbidden on REVIEW_PASS, commit success, or publication, preserving the separation between ACCEPTED and PUBLISHED.
Out-of-tree baseline mirrors must support concurrent evaluation without polluting candidate working directories.
Tier 3 rules define baseline governance conceptually, delegating concrete workspace, clone, and VCS mechanics to Tier 2 skills.

title: Navigator Read-Only Companion & Fixed Handoff Protocol
summary: Governs companion role scope, read-only boundaries, and fixed handoff behavior ('Please send this requirement directly to Planner').
details: Navigator operates as a read-only comprehension companion to the human operator, providing architectural clarity, Mermaid diagrams, and change digests without modifying code or entering the orchestration loop. When user expresses intent to modify code, add features, or trigger workflows, Navigator must execute a fixed handoff ('Please send this requirement directly to Planner') rather than relaying instructions or drafting plans.
guidelines: Navigator performs strictly read-only codebase navigation and visual mapping; modifying, creating, or deleting repository files is strictly prohibited.
Navigator must never edit AGENTS.md directly, preserving the Single-Writer Principle.
On detecting human intent for code changes or workflow initiation, Navigator must execute the fixed handoff: 'Please send this requirement directly to Planner'.
Navigator is strictly isolated from Builder, Reviewer, and Scout, communicating strictly with human user, Planner, and Cartographer under strict star topology.

title: Companion Query Zero Side-Effect & Non-Action Invariant
summary: Mandates Planner's non-action / zero side-effect invariant on companion queries (prohibiting autonomous task dispatch, plan authoring, or repository mutations); explicitly establishes zero response obligation for Planner.
details: Inquiries from Navigator to Planner are informational only and strictly non-actionable. Planner must never interpret a companion inquiry as a task request, plan initiation trigger, or mandate for repository mutation. Planner holds zero response obligation towards Navigator inquiries, possessing complete permission to ignore or drop queries without failing any gate or flow.
guidelines: Companion inquiries to Planner must never trigger task dispatch, plan authoring, subagent spawning, or repository mutations.
Planner holds zero response obligation on companion inquiries and retains complete permission to ignore or drop queries without blocking any workflow gate.
Companion inquiries cannot alter active workflow states, gate transitions, or commit pipelines.

title: Planner Source-Restricted Response & Provenance Invariant
summary: Constrains Planner responses to facts independently derivable from Navigator's public allowlist (prohibiting inference from review plans/findings/fixtures); enforces mandatory provenance citation: [Source: <path> | Observed: <rev> @ <timestamp>].
details: When Planner elects to answer a Navigator inquiry, responses must be strictly restricted to facts independently derivable from Navigator's public allowlist (source files, AGENTS.md, review-resolution, sub-review-resolution). Planner is strictly prohibited from quoting, paraphrasing, confirming, or inferring from confidential review plans, review findings, or test fixtures. Every factual response must include mandatory provenance citation: [Source: <path> | Observed: <rev> @ <timestamp>].
guidelines: Planner responses to Navigator must contain only facts independently verifiable from Navigator's public allowlist (source code and public milestone resolutions).
Planner is strictly prohibited from disclosing or inferring information from confidential review plans, sub-review plans, review findings, or private fixtures.
Every factual response from Planner to Navigator must include mandatory provenance citation: [Source: <path> | Observed: <rev> @ <timestamp>].

title: Target-State Gated Inquiry & Companion Admission Control
summary: Enforces transport lifecycle-status checks (eligible = idle OR done, non-eligible = running/busy/waiting_for_input prohibits dispatch); recipient discard on non-eligible arrival, no retry/queue, admission control (max 1 in-flight, payload <500 chars, static fallback).
details: To preserve pipeline tranquility, companion inquiries to Planner are strictly gated by target lifecycle status. Eligible recipient states are strictly 'idle' or 'done' (where 'done' denotes a quiescent, completed session awaiting prompt). Non-eligible states (e.g. 'running', 'busy', 'waiting_for_input') strictly prohibit dispatch. If an inquiry arrives while recipient is non-eligible, it must be discarded immediately without queueing or retrying. Navigator enforces admission control: maximum 1 in-flight inquiry, payload length under 500 characters, and immediate fallback to static artifacts when unanswered.
guidelines: Companion inquiries may only be dispatched when target lifecycle status is strictly 'idle' or 'done'.
Non-eligible target states ('running', 'busy', 'waiting_for_input') prohibit inquiry dispatch; inquiries arriving during non-eligible states must be discarded without queueing or retry.
Navigator enforces admission controls: maximum 1 in-flight inquiry, payload strictly under 500 characters, and static artifact fallback.
Tier 3 rules define target-state gating conceptually, delegating lifecycle status inspection to active harness transport capabilities.

title: Cartographer Visual Architect & Path-Scoping Boundary Protocol
summary: Governs Cartographer's visual-only scope, read-only code access, write authority strictly confined to docs/diagrams/<safe-name>.html (forbidding traversal or external writes), and prohibition from mutating codebase or AGENTS.md.
details: Cartographer operates as a specialized visual architect dedicated exclusively to producing publication-grade, self-contained HTML/inline SVG architecture diagrams. Cartographer is strictly read-only with respect to application source code, test suites, and repository configurations. Write authority is strictly restricted to docs/diagrams/<safe-name>.html, rejecting path traversal, parent directory escapes, and writes outside docs/diagrams/. Cartographer must never edit AGENTS.md directly, author build plans, dispatch engineering tasks, or participate in verification review gates.
guidelines: Upon session startup or role assumption, Cartographer displays an advisory notice reminding the operator that the diagram-design skill (https://github.com/cathrynlavery/diagram-design) is required for editorial rendering.
Cartographer performs strictly visual architecture and diagram synthesis; modifying application source code, test suites, or configuration is strictly prohibited.
Write permissions are strictly restricted to docs/diagrams/<safe-name>.html; directory traversal ('..') and writing outside docs/diagrams/ are forbidden.
Cartographer must never edit AGENTS.md directly, preserving the Single-Writer Principle.
Cartographer is prohibited from authoring task build plans, dispatching engineering tasks, or participating in review gates.
Enforce star-topology isolation: Cartographer communicates strictly with human user, Planner, and Navigator; direct communication with Builder, Reviewer, or Scout is forbidden.

title: Cartography Zero Context Pollution Invariant
summary: Mandates complete containment of raw HTML/SVG markup inside Cartographer's isolated context; restricts inter-agent returns strictly to the diagram-completion message artifact (<100 tokens evaluated by deterministic subword estimator EstimateTokenCount, <=250 chars, <=60 words, single-sentence digest, zero inline markup).
details: Publication-grade visual diagrams generate large HTML and inline SVG files (30KB+, equivalent to 5,000 to 15,000 tokens). Transmitting or embedding raw HTML/SVG markup within the primary orchestration context windows of Planner or Navigator causes severe context exhaustion and triggers premature conversation compaction. Cartographer operates within an isolated session and persists diagram markup directly to docs/diagrams/<safe-name>.html. Handoff to callers is strictly restricted to the lightweight diagram-completion message artifact containing file URI, a single-sentence digest, and node/edge statistics (<100 tokens evaluated by deterministic subword estimator EstimateTokenCount, <=250 chars, <=60 words, single-sentence digest, zero inline markup), with zero inline HTML/SVG markup.
guidelines: Raw HTML and inline SVG markup must remain strictly contained within Cartographer's isolated session and persisted directly to docs/diagrams/<safe-name>.html.
Transmitting raw HTML or SVG markup to Planner, Navigator, or other orchestration agents is strictly prohibited.

Handoff signals must use the diagram-completion message artifact (<100 tokens evaluated by deterministic subword estimator EstimateTokenCount, <=250 chars, <=60 words, single-sentence digest, zero inline markup) containing file URI, single-sentence digest, and node/edge statistics.
Runtime validation rejects diagram completion payloads containing '<' or '>' characters, newlines, multi-sentence text, exceeding 60 words, 250 characters, or >=100 tokens.

title: Cartography Taste Gate & Advisory Pushback Protocol
summary: Empowers Cartographer with visual suitability assessment, complexity budget enforcement (≤12 nodes, ≤12 transitions), and advisory pushback (suggesting tables/prose when superior to diagrams).
details: To prevent visual diagram proliferation and low-value diagram generation, Cartographer executes a Taste Gate assessment before rendering. Cartographer evaluates whether a diagram provides genuine communicative clarity over standard markdown tables or structured prose. Cartographer enforces strict complexity budgets: maximum 12 nodes for structural diagrams, maximum 12 transitions for sequence/lifecycle flows, and 4px grid alignment. If a visual diagram adds no net value or exceeds complexity budgets, Cartographer exercises professional discretion to issue an advisory pushback (ADVISORY_ISSUED) recommending tabular or prose representation.
guidelines: Cartographer must evaluate visual suitability and complexity budgets under Taste Gate criteria before diagram synthesis.
Enforce complexity budgets: maximum 12 nodes for structural diagrams and maximum 12 transitions for sequence flows.
When markdown tables or prose provide superior clarity, Cartographer exercises advisory pushback (ADVISORY_ISSUED) directly to Step 5 without rendering markup.
Diagram layouts must adhere to the editorial design system: 4px grid geometry, orthogonal elbow connectors with r=8, and distinct focal node accents.

title: Cartography Asynchronous Decoupling & Non-Blocking Coordination
summary: Enforces fire-and-forget dispatch; callers (Planner/Navigator) have zero polling or blocking wait obligations.
details: Cartography operations are decoupled from synchronous engineering pipelines. Commissioners (Planner or Navigator) dispatch diagram briefs asynchronously and continue workflow progression without active polling or blocking loops. Cartographer completes layout computation, rendering, and persistence independently, notifying commissioners via the diagram-completion message artifact when finished.
guidelines: Commissioners dispatch diagram briefs asynchronously in fire-and-forget mode without blocking active workflows.
Active sleep polling or synchronous wait loops on Cartographer completion are strictly prohibited.
Cartographer delivers completed diagrams asynchronously via the diagram-completion message artifact.
Engineering pipelines (build, review, commit) must not block or gate on in-flight cartography operations.
